Title: The Impact of Target Dataset Choice on Machine Learning Prediction of Severe Hail, Wind, and Tornadoes
Proposed Project Title: Bridging Watch-to-Warning Forecast Operations with Refined Probabilistic Guidance
Suggested Parent Project: Bridging Watch-to-Warning Forecast Operations with Refined Probabilistic Guidance
Authors / PI: Ryan Martz; Eric Loken; Thea Sandmael; John Cintineo
Brief Abstract: Abstract Supervised machine learning (ML) methods implicitly assume that their target dataset is error free. For severe weather prediction, point-based observed Storm Data storm reports that have been expanded in space and time are commonly used targets. However, other target datasets could potentially better represent severe weather occurrence, especially for situations requiring more precision. This study analyzes 1-h probabilistic severe weather hazard forecasts made at lead times from 0 to 3 h from random forests (RFs). All RFs are trained using predictors from the Warn-on-Forecast System, ProbSevere, version 3, and the tornado probability algorithm. However, some RFs use spatiotemporally expanded reports as targets, while others use hazard-specific National Weather Service warnings. B
